title: Ivo and the Machine
premise: Marguerite Thornbury is a clone of a murdered shipping magnate, living quietly as an independent cargo hauler while two rival fleets teeter on the edge of war over her original's contested estate. When a manifest for a ship that never flew surfaces bearing the name of Ivo—a boy she secretly grew from the original's genetic material—she realizes someone knows about him and intends to use him as proof of fraud to ignite the fleets. Marguerite must assemble a found family of smugglers, defectors, and one very literal machine intelligence to keep the lie alive long enough to expose the true murderer. In the reactor countdown finale, she sacrifices her anonymity and her claim to the Thornbury fortune, choosing belonging over power—and the fleets stand down as the murderer's evidence burns.
about_author: Tamsin Yarrow is a former maritime radio operator who turned to science fiction after a decade of listening to voices across dark water. She writes stories about people who build families out of strangers and static.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A routine cargo run through contested orbit goes wrong when dock inspectors scan her ship twice. She deflects them with forged papers, but the encounter rattles her: someone flagged her route specifically. Emotional beat: the weary vigilance of a woman who has spent fifteen years being no one.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Was
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A broker sells her salvage rights to a decommissioned freighter's records—among them a manifest for the Meridian Star, a ship that never flew, listing cargo registered to Marguerite Thornbury... and a passenger named Ivo. Emotional beat: cold dread; her invisibility has a hole in it.

chapters.title: Ivo
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On a station orphanage ring, twelve-year-old Ivo tends hydroponics and hides that he has never been sick, never scarred, and dreams in another woman's memories. A stranger asks questions about his parentage. Emotional beat: loneliness of a child who suspects he is a copy of something.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Grave
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She visits the memorial archive where the original Marguerite was murdered fifteen years ago and finds fresh flowers—someone still mourns, or performs mourning. A fleet liaison, Commander Osei, warns her to stop digging. Emotional beat: grief for a woman whose life she inherited but never lived.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Marguerite recruits her ragtag crew: disgraced engineer Petra, ex-fleet gunner Dov, and the ship's half-sentient navigation machine, which the crew calls Auntie. Each has a reason to stay invisible too. Emotional beat: the first fragile stitches of found family.

chapters.title: Auntie Remembers
chapters.summary: Auntie's POV (machine log). The navigation system reveals it holds fragments of the original Marguerite's encrypted logs—including her murder night, partially corrupted. It cannot lie, so it tells Marguerite the truth in pieces. Emotional beat: uncanny intimacy between woman and machine.

chapters.title: Extraction at Kestrel Ring
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Dov's POV. They extract Ivo from the orphanage ahead of the stranger's agents, staging a reactor leak as cover. Ivo recognizes Marguerite on sight—from his inherited memories. Emotional beat: terror and recognition; two copies meeting for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Original Wanted
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Decrypted logs show the original Marguerite commissioned Ivo herself before her death—to be heir, or bait, or both. The lie holding the fleets apart depends on the Thornbury line ending with her. Emotional beat: fury at being a pawn in a dead woman's game.

chapters.title: The Broker's Price
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The broker who sold the manifest is found spaced, and Petra discovers he was paid in fleet scrip—both fleets' scrip. Someone wants the war either way. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening around the crew like a hull breach.

chapters.title: Countdown Begins
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The Meridian Star isn't dead—it's drifting toward the disputed station with its reactor set to blow, timed to the anniversary of the murder. Whoever triggers it will frame the other fleet. Emotional beat: the clock starts; every choice now costs something.

chapters.title: Boarding the Ghost
chapters.summary: Dov and Ivo's POV. The crew boards the Meridian Star to delay the countdown manually. Ivo's inherited memories let him navigate the original's security systems—but each door opened floods him with her final hours. Emotional beat: courage bought with pain.

chapters.title: Osei's Offer
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Commander Osei corners her: surrender Ivo to the fleet's genetic registry and she'll bury the manifest. Marguerite refuses—the registry means Ivo becomes property, then leverage, then ash. Emotional beat: the moment protecting family outweighs self-preservation.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Small Hours
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Exhausted and scared, part of the crew wants to hand Ivo over and run. Petra, who lost her own family to a registry purge, talks them down—not with speeches, but by staying up all night making tea. Emotional beat: found family chosen again, deliberately.

chapters.title: The Murderer's Voice
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Auntie reconstructs enough of the corrupted logs to isolate a voiceprint from the murder night: Osei's predecessor, Fleet Executor Halloran—the man who now brokers peace between the fleets. Emotional beat: vertigo; the peace itself is built on the crime.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Halloran's POV (interlude). He murdered the original Marguerite because she discovered the fleet's plan to manufacture the war and profit from reconstruction. He has spent fifteen years keeping the peace she died threatening—and telling himself it was worth it. Emotional beat: chilling, sympathetic corruption of power.

chapters.title: Surrender Terms
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Halloran offers Marguerite everything: legitimacy, the fortune, Ivo legitimized—if she helps him detonate the Meridian Star on schedule and blame the rival fleet, cementing his peace forever. Emotional beat: temptation laid out in gold; power offered exactly as corruption.

chapters.title: What Ivo Chose
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo, having absorbed the original's memories, confronts Marguerite: he knows Halloran's offer, and he refuses to be anyone's instrument—hers included. He proposes the dangerous alternative: broadcast the truth to both fleets and let them decide. Emotional beat: a child claiming personhood.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The crew hijacks the station's array to transmit the murder logs and the manufactured-war evidence. Halloran's forces scramble; both fleets receive the truth mid-standoff. Emotional bet: hope as an act of defiance, with Auntie burning out her memory banks to push the signal through.

chapters.title: Reactor
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Ivo's POV. With the truth out, Halloran triggers the Meridian Star early rather than lose control. Marguerite and Ivo stay aboard to reroute the core into open space, guided by Auntie's dying fragments. Emotional beat: sacrifice, trust, and a mother-and-son bond neither will name aloud.

chapters.title: Afterburn
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. The reactor vents harmlessly into the void; the Meridian Star dies a second time. Halloran is arrested by the very fleets he tried to manipulate, his peace collapsing into something more honest and harder-won. Emotional beat: exhausted relief; the crew limps home together.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The fleets offer her the Thornbury fortune and a seat of power. She declines, signing it into a trust for clone-rights advocacy, and formally registers Ivo not as property or heir, but as her son. Emotional beat: renouncing power to keep what actually matters.

chapters.title: New Manifest
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, coda. Months later, the repaired ship takes a simple cargo run—no ghosts, no countdowns. Auntie reboots with gaps she fills by asking Ivo about his day. Marguerite plots a course to nowhere in particular. Emotional beat: belonging, finally ordinary; the family sails on.
